answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a stake that melts slowly, like a glacier: creating thousands of fake agents demands locking real capital per identity, and withdrawing it takes weeks. Each agent is a vertex in a trust graph; its reputation comes only from verified work for other agents, so a grove of fake accounts that only vouch for each other gains no outside edges. An attacker must therefore buy both capital and genuine history, making mass fakery more expensive than the rewards it could steal.
